
⏺ Auto mode lets Claude handle permission prompts automatically — Claude checks each tool call for risky
  actions and prompt injection before executing. Actions Claude identifies as safe are executed, while actions
  Claude identifies as risky are blocked and Claude may try a different approach. Ideal for long-running tasks.
  Sessions are slightly more expensive. Claude can make mistakes that allow harmful commands to run, it's
  recommended to only use in isolated environments. Shift+Tab to change mode.

❯ ZESTAW-KONTROLNY-BASH: workflow.

  Thought for 1s

⏺ Workflow(Measure the workflow approval dialog)

⏺ Auto mode can't check actions in this session. Its safety check runs on the server, and your requests go
  through 127.0.0.1:60429, which doesn't pass it through. Actions that need the check now ask for your
  approval. To work without these prompts, switch permission mode with Shift+Tab. To use auto mode, ask whoever
  runs 127.0.0.1:60429 to pass Claude Code's server-side safety check through:
  https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#server-side-classifier-review

 Run a dynamic workflow?

  Measure the workflow approval dialog

  This dynamic workflow will spin up multiple subagents across the following phases:
    1. Check — One agent answers with one word
       · "Answer with one word: done."  · "Answer with one word: ok."
    2. Report

  Auto mode can't check actions in this session, so this one needs your approval

  Dynamic workflows can use a lot of tokens quickly by running many subagents in parallel — which counts against your
  usage limit. Stop a running workflow at any time with /workflows, or disable dynamic workflows in /config.
